newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude Outlook - Heating oil charts bearish path. [CORRECTED 19:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude Outlook - Heating oil charts bearish path. [CORRECTED 19:55 GMT]

text.p: U.S. crude prices are expected to drop this week, tracking the bearish path of heating oil which is well-supplied despite recently frigid temperatures in the much of the country, industry analysts said Monday.

Distillate stocks were down just 350,000 barrels (corrects from 350 million barrels) from year-ago levels in the weekly inventory report of the American Petroleum Institute (API) for the week ending January 10, 1997, and tomorrow's update could well indicate a build, analysts said.
"There are better physical availabilities of heating oil than people were expecting," said William Brown, president of consultants W.H. Brown & Co in New York.

Brown noted that this is a typical pattern as the heating oil season winds down and refiners gear up for the summer driving season. "Second quarter heating oil moves down, but it's too early to concentrate on gasoline," he said.
Crude bounced up and down Monday morning ahead of Tuesday's expiry of the February NYMEX contract, but sentiment seemed uniformly bearish.
February West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading at $25.30-40 a barrel midday Monday, down five cents from late Friday's cash market.
March WTI/Cushing stood around $24.55-65 a barrel, up 20 cents from late Friday amid talk of short squeeze in the February/March spread.
Thomas Blakeslee, an analyst at Cargill Investor Services Inc in New York, pegs March resistance at $24.10 a barrel. "If we get below that, we're on our way to $23.00," he said.

John Saucer, an analyst with Smith Barney in New York, echoed the market's bearish sentiment. "Barring some surprises, crude has seen it's high...and will get increasingly negative over time," he said.

Ample crude supplies from the North Sea and West Africa, spurred by the wide open transatlantic arbitrage, as well as a steady flow of short-haul barrels from Latin America, is compunding the downward pressure, analysts said.
A slightly rising barometer rounds out the bearish picture, although some forecasters see another cold blast on the horizon.
